messages:
leo: FYI seeing intermittent nvme queue_wait spikes on a handful of hosts in us-west2 around 01:14 UTC, GPU attach latencies jump and autoscaler hesitates. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/io/host-iops?var-region=us-west2

anya: same, about 7 hosts. pattern looks like short scrub bursts overlapping with batch warmup. devices are FlashZ-7 series, small 400GB partitions.

chris: dug into janitor logs, found concurrent scrub jobs started at same minute across rack. scrub_concurrency was 5 from the recent operator flag change. sample:

```
2026-03-20T01:14:02Z janitor[231]: starting scrub nvme0n1p1
2026-03-20T01:14:03Z janitor[231]: read error EAGAIN, backoff
2026-03-20T01:14:05Z janitor[231]: queue_wait=380ms
```

leo: quick patch: applied node-level annotation `redwood.io/scrub-priority=low` to affected nodes and reduced concurrency to 1 on them. also cordoned 2 nodes with worst queue_wait.

anya: can we add a short-term allocator rule to prefer nodes reporting nvme.queue_wait < 100ms for GPU attaches? that buys us time while we adjust scrub schedules.

chris: done. pushed routing change to allocator: prefer nodes where `nvme.queue_wait_p95 < 100`. Monitoring now.

ops-bot: [alert] attach_wait.us-west2 reduced; affected hosts decreased from 7 -> 1. Incident window 01:14-01:18 UTC.

leo: follow-ups: 1) revert the global scrub_concurrency flag change from last release and roll it out as a per-cluster opt-in; 2) implement thermal/queue-aware janitor backoff policy (RFC); 3) add Optimize rule to recommend staggering scrubs by rack during scheduled batch scaleups.

anya: also flagging FlashZ-7 firmware — multiple hosts show increased retry counts. file a hardware ticket with vendors.

chris: will open the vendor ticket and schedule a controlled scrub-canary during low-traffic window next Tuesday.
